draft.title: Why countries trade
card: No country has every resource or skill it needs. Resources include land, minerals, water, climate and workers' skills.
Countries have different resources and skills. One may have plenty of farmland, while another has little farmland but many skilled workers.
A country sells to others what it has spare, which is more than its own people need.
It buys what it cannot make at all, or cannot make as well or as cheaply as another country can.
draft.remember: Countries trade because they differ: they sell their spare goods and buy what others make better or cheaper.

a.q: Which is the best reason why countries trade with each other?
opts: They have different resources and skills
They all have the same resources and skills
Each country can make everything it needs
Trade is the only way a country can earn money
a.why: Countries differ in what they have and can do, so each can sell its spare goods and buy what it lacks. The idea that countries have the same resources is wrong, because then there would be little to swap.
a.clue: Think about what countries have and lack.

b.q: Norway has lots of cold sea and a big fishing industry, but its climate is too cold to grow oranges. Why might Norway trade with Spain?
opts: To sell spare fish and buy oranges it cannot grow
To sell oranges that it has grown in excess
To stop Spain from catching its own fish
To buy fish that Norway cannot catch itself
b.why: Norway has more fish than it needs and a climate that cannot grow oranges. Trade lets it sell the fish and buy the oranges. Selling oranges is wrong because Norway cannot grow them.
b.clue: What does Norway have spare, and what does it lack?

a.best: They have different resources and skills

b.best: To sell spare fish and buy oranges it cannot grow
